primary_meaning: Spiritual unfaithfulness or idolatry (covenant adultery against God, often depicted as Israel or the people of God acting as a harlot by pursuing false gods or worldly powers)

alternatives.meaning: Literal sexual immorality or cultic prostitution without metaphor (treated as straightforward ethical prohibition rather than symbol)
Political alliances or dependence on foreign nations (treated as a form of unfaithfulness overlapping with but distinct from pure idolatry)
Apostate or corrupt religious institution (e.g., the harlot as the false church or Babylon as ecclesiastical Rome in historicist Protestant readings)
basis: interpretive tradition linking to 2 Thessalonians 2 and papal critiques

alternatives.meaning: Economic exploitation, luxury, or commercial seduction of the nations (especially Babylon the great as imperial commerce)

notes: The prophetic metaphor of whoredom for idolatry/covenant breach is the dominant and long-settled symbolic reading across mainstream Jewish and Christian interpretation of the relevant texts; literal sexual readings coexist but are not the primary symbolic assignment. Secondary applications (political, institutional, economic) remain subsidiary elaborations of the same unfaithfulness motif rather than fully independent meanings.
